newsitem.title: USA: Knowles signs bill hiking Alaska tobacco tax.
newsitem.headline: Knowles signs bill hiking Alaska tobacco tax.

text.p: Brandishing a crushed pack of Camel cigarettes, Alaska Gov. Tony Knowles signed a bill Wednesday hiking the state's tobacco tax by 71 cents a pack.
"This is going to be the straw that helps break Joe Camel's back," Knowles said in a ceremony at an Anchorage middle school.
The bill, which takes effect in October, will give Alaska the nation's highest tobacco tax, raising the 29-cent rate to $1 a pack for cigarettes and a similar amount for other tobacco products.
The Democratic governor told applauding students that increasing the tax would reduce youth tobacco use.
The tobacco tax increase is expected to raise about $33 million a year for the state. Alaska has the nation's second-highest rate of adult smoking, behind only Nevada, Knowles said.

Alaska teen-agers also have high rates of tobacco use, he said. About 21 percent of Alaska high school students become frequent cigarette smokers, compared to the national average of 14 percent, he said.

Attending the bill-signing ceremony were several legislators and health activists who had advocated the bill as a measure to reduce teen tobacco use, and two former governors. Walter Hickel, a Republican, and Bill Sheffield, a Democrat, had campaigned in favor of the tobacco-tax hike.
